_help: reports: what must be ready before you can submit at the SRAG console. 'task' is work at a station (detector, vehicle, medical) or 'astronaut' (debrief the visiting astronaut); 'signoff' is a coworker's name; 'stamps' lists managers (boss ids from office.json) whose approval stamp it needs, and management reviews add more during the round. Coworkers: 'location' is [column, row] in office.json; 'wants' (optional) is an item they need first (coffee, timesheet, r13, memos, dosimetry); 'gives' hands you an item; 'look' sets sprite colours (extras: long_hair, glasses ('thick' for thick rims), beard, mustache, bald, headset, tie, flightsuit, rainbow_jacket, bracelets). Helpers can have a 'perk': freeze_managers, flare_watch, fast_reviews, jeopardy (uses 'quiz'; answer is 1, 2 or 3), people_person, remote_access, sim_priority, gcr_model. 'patrol' makes someone walk a loop. Conversation traps: 'black_hole' (pulls you in when you get close), 'physics' (triggers when you talk to them three times in quick succession, then walks you to their 'home' spot) and 'drop_in' (arrives from the elevator now and then and seeks you out).

lines: 🗣️ Nic: Ugh, Eddie just added another form to the radiation tracking stack.
🗣️ Nic: Sometimes I wonder if a solar flare could take out this whole floor... and our paperwork with it.
npc_encounters.sign: Fine, I'll sign off on the Weekly Report. If the flare takes out the paperwork, at least my signature goes down with it.

lines: 🗣️ Katie W.: If Clifton asks me about my timesheet one more time, I’m launching him into a supernova.
🗣️ Katie W.: At least if the sun explodes, I won’t have to finish my TPS reports.

wants.ask: Sign off on the TPS Report? Sure, right after you rescue my timesheet. It's jammed in the copy room, the south-west corner office.
wants.thanks: My timesheet! Clifton can audit THAT. TPS Report signed off, cover sheet and all.

npc_encounters.title: Known hazard
lines: 🗣️ Kevin: Eddie says if I touch the Mars dosimeter again, he’ll reassign me to the printer queue.
🗣️ Kevin: I swear, I’ve had more meaningful conversations with cosmic rays than with Clifton.

wants.ask: I can't sign off on a Mission Dose Report before coffee. The break room is in the middle of the floor, behind the elevators.
wants.thanks: Oh, that's the good stuff. Mission Dose Report: signed.

lines: So, funny story about the Mars dosimeter. It starts in 2019...
Did I ever tell you about my commute? There's a left turn you won't believe.
Hang on, this ties back to the dosimeter thing. Sort of.
Anyway, where was I? Oh right, the beginning.
You know what the problem with cosmic rays is? Okay, there are several...
🗣️ John FM: I told Eddie I was exposed to gamma... he said ‘Did you file an R-13 for that?’
🗣️ John FM: If Clifton asks ‘what is it you do here?’ again, I’ll tell him: I absorb solar storms... emotionally.

wants.ask: I'll sign off on your Astronaut Dose Report if you grab me a blank R-13 from Eddie's filing cabinets. His office is on the north side. Don't let him see you.
wants.thanks: A fresh R-13. Smells like bureaucracy. Your Astronaut Dose Report is signed.

npc_encounters.title: IT
lines: 🗣️ Ryan R: Have you tried turning the solar storm off and on again?
🗣️ Ryan R: The printer isn't broken. It's a physics problem. Everything is a physics problem.

wants.ask: Did you put in a ticket? No ticket, no fix. Write one on a memo and bring it to me.
wants.thanks: Ticket received. Pushing a mandatory update to every management laptop... now. That buys you about fifteen seconds.

lines: Okay, so: a muon hits the top of the atmosphere at 0.998c. How long does it think this hallway is?
Let me just draw this on the whiteboard. You'll love it. It has integrals.
Ignore air resistance. And the walls. And your deadline.
So, assume a spherical astronaut in a vacuum...
Wait, I think the sign is wrong. Let's start over from the top.

npc_encounters.title: Mission Control Console
lines: 🗣️ Janet: I've got the sun on one monitor and Eddie's forms on the other. Guess which one's scarier.
🗣️ Janet: We are GO for coffee. NO-GO for Clifton's timesheet audit.
npc_encounters.perk_line: I'll patch you into the console loop. You'll hear about flares early, and I'll get the crew sheltering sooner.

npc_encounters.title: Console operations
lines: 🗣️ Jennifer M: The console room runs on caffeine and checklists.
🗣️ Jennifer M: If a run gets queued behind one of Ryan's physics jobs, it's queued forever.
npc_encounters.perk_line: I'll bump your vehicle dose run to the front of the queue. Twice as fast. Don't tell Ryan.

npc_encounters.title: Console IT
lines: 🗣️ Mark L: Console IT. If it beeps, it's mine.
🗣️ Mark L: Fifteen monitors, one keyboard, zero problems. Okay, two problems.
npc_encounters.perk_line: I'll set you up with remote access to the vehicle run. Go do your other stuff; it'll keep cranking.

npc_encounters.title: Spreadsheets
lines: 🗣️ Steve J: Everything is a spreadsheet if you believe in yourself.
🗣️ Steve J: Eddie asked for a legend on my color-coded dose tracker. I gave him a pivot table. He hasn't spoken to me since.
npc_encounters.perk_line: Hand me your reports. Pivot tables, conditional formatting, frozen header row... There. Management will approve these twice as fast.

npc_encounters.title: Dosimeters
lines: 🗣️ Ramona: Badge on, badge facing out. Every dosimeter tells a story. Yours is a thriller.
🗣️ Ramona: I read dosimeters the way other people read tea leaves.
npc_encounters.give_line: Here are the crew's dosimeter readings. Every badge, every day. Don't spill coffee on them.

npc_encounters.title: Cosmic radiation modeling
lines: 🗣️ Serkan G: I ran the galactic cosmic ray model again last night. For fun. Want to see the spectra?
🗣️ Serkan G: My Little Pony taught me friendship is magic. Transport codes taught me shielding is mass.
🗣️ Serkan G: I'm in my modeling era.
🗣️ Serkan G: These friendship bracelets? Traded them at the concert. This one says HZE.
npc_encounters.perk_line: Vehicle dose? I already modeled it. Twice. Here, take my run, it's half done.

npc_encounters.title: Galactic cosmic ray model
lines: 🗣️ Pat O: I once told a joke about a cosmic ray. It went right through everyone.
🗣️ Pat O: Back in my day we tracked cosmic rays with a cloud chamber and a lot of patience. Mostly patience.
🗣️ Pat O: Heavy ions. Still lighter than my thesis committee.
🗣️ Pat O: My GCR model has been around the galaxy a few times. Like me. Your vehicle run? Oh, I wouldn't know.
🗣️ Pat O: Remember when the solar minimum was a minimum? Good times. Good, low-flux times.
🗣️ Pat O: A neutron walks into a bar and asks the price. The bartender says: for you, no charge.
🗣️ Pat O: They don't make particles like they used to. Well, they do. That's the problem.
🗣️ Pat O: Help with your report? Ha! Did I ever tell you about the 1989 solar storm? What a year.

npc_encounters.title: Jeopardy Aficionado
lines: 🗣️ Amir B: I'll take Space Weather for 800.
🗣️ Amir B: Remember: answer in the form of a question.

quiz.clue: This SI unit of dose equivalent is worth 100 rem.
This SI unit of absorbed dose is one joule per kilogram.
Earth's belts of trapped radiation are named for this Iowa physicist.
The huge solar particle event of August 1972 struck between these two missions.
Mission Control at Johnson Space Center is in this numbered building.
This weak spot in Earth's magnetic field gives the ISS a radiation bump on many orbits.
choices: What is the South Atlantic Anomaly?

quiz.clue: On a space weather alert, CME stands for this.
choices: What is a cosmic microwave echo?
What is a coronal mass ejection?
What is a crew medical exam?

quiz.clue: This station has had people aboard continuously since November 2000.
PC LOAD LETTER baffled the staff in this 1999 office comedy.

npc_encounters.title: People Person
lines: 🗣️ Mark S: I'm a people person. I take the paperwork to management so the engineers don't have to.
🗣️ Mark S: What would you say I do here? I talk to Eddie and Clifton, so you don't have to.
npc_encounters.perk_line: If Eddie or Clifton corner you, I'll step in and smooth it over. I have people skills.

npc_encounters.title: Visiting crew member
lines: 🗣️ Astronaut: Busy day? I've had busier. In orbit.
🗣️ Astronaut: You folks keep us safe up there. I tell everyone. Mostly about me, but also about you.
debrief: Dose? I prefer to think of it as bonus experience.
I already finished my debrief. And yours, probably.
My resting heart rate is 38. During launch.
Let me tell you about my last spacewalk. All seven hours of it.
Shielding is great. I'm basically shielding for everyone else's morale.

npc_encounters.title: Former manager
lines: 🗣️ Neil Z: Oh, hi. Just passing through. As one does.
Why did the proton get promoted? Positive attitude. ...Anyway.
Back when I ran this group, we computed dose by hand. Uphill. In a magnetosphere.
Neutrinos walk into a bar. They pass right through. That's the whole joke.
I used to manage this group. Now I manage my expectations.
Have you tried the new coffee? Me neither. Good talk.
A watched dosimeter never accumulates. Or does it? Think about it.
Busy. The dose numbers are due today.
Has anyone seen my dosimeter? It was on my lanyard a second ago.
Flare alerts all morning. My coffee's gone cold three times.
I'm not ignoring you, I'm compiling.
If Clifton asks, I've been here since seven.
The proton flux plot looks like my blood pressure.
Do you know where the good stapler went?
I'm three meetings behind and it's not even lunch.
Eddie added a field to the form. The form about forms.
The printer only works if you say please. Out loud.
My shielding model converged! Oh, wait. No.
I brought donuts. They're gone. Story of my life.
Building 30 called. They want the numbers yesterday.
Every time someone says 'quick question', a sievert dies.
I'm on hold with IT. Ryan says it's a physics problem.
The crew's fine. The crew is always fine. We make sure of that.
Have you seen Neil? He was here, said something about neutrinos, and left.
Kevin got me for forty minutes this morning. Stay strong.
I color-coded my calendar. Now it's just all red.
Lunch? I don't know her.
Does anyone know the Wi-Fi password? It changed. Again.

puns: 🗣️ You hear someone mutter: ‘I was told there would be no ionizing radiation...’
🗣️ A sigh echoes from the cubicle: ‘If someone steals my lead shielding again, I’m gonna burn this place down.’
🗣️ A voice jokes: ‘I deal with solar proton events... not people.’
🗣️ Overheard: ‘Yeah, I’m gonna need you to stay during the coronal mass ejection...’
🗣️ Someone’s yelling: ‘PC Load Letter?! What does that even mean in a vacuum?!’
🗣️ Overheard: ‘Ryan, the printer's doing it again.’ ‘Did you file a ticket?’
🗣️ From the cubicles: ‘What is... a coronal mass ejection?’ ‘Correct!’
🗣️ Someone mutters: ‘Steve put the coffee budget in a pivot table and now nobody's allowed coffee.’
🗣️ From the console room: ‘Serkan, is that a pony on your jacket?’ ‘It's a cutie mark. Also, your shielding model is wrong.’
🗣️ Someone whispers: ‘Don't make eye contact with Kevin. Don't make eye contact with Kevin.’
🗣️ Overheard near a whiteboard: ‘...and that's why the muon thinks the hallway is shorter.’
🗣️ From the north-east office: ‘Pat, does your cosmic ray model run on anything newer than Fortran 77?’ ‘Run? It strolls.’

spot: Hold on. Is that an unfiled Weekly Report?
You there! I've got a form for that.
Got a second? It's about the radiation tracking stack.
hear: Hm? Who's out there without a hall pass form?
Was that a printer jam? That needs a form.
lost: ...I'll just add a form about that.
Fine. I'll put it in the stack.
catch: Did you file a dose report for that? Here's the addendum, the appendix and a cover sheet.
This goes on the radiation tracking stack. In triplicate.
stunned: Ooh, a memo. I must read it in full.
A memo! Is this the new revision?
review: Let's see... dose units, check. Font size... hmm.
Did you use the new template? ...You did. Huh.
approve: Fine. Approved. Don't make it a habit.

spot: Got a minute? It's about your timesheet...
Ah, just the person I wanted to audit.
hear: Someone there? I have a quick question.
lost: Let's put a pin in that.
catch: So... what is it you do here, exactly?
Your timesheet says 'absorbing solar storms'. That's not a billing code.
Your TPS Report is missing the new cover sheet.
stunned: A memo? I'll need to cross-reference this.
Hmm, interesting memo. Let me just...
review: Let me cross-reference this with your timesheet...
Interesting. And what is it this report does here?
approve: Approved. I'll circle back on the font.
STAMP. Let's touch base next week.
